subject: Order Form redlines — notice ladder, auto-renew escape, and TFC fallback
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Samantha Price <samantha.price@novahealth.com>
Cc: procurement@novahealth.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Order Form redlines — notice ladder, auto-renew escape, and TFC fallback

Hi all,

Attaching the latest order form redline (OF-Redline-v3.docx). Legal and procurement items left outstanding:

1) Auto-renew trigger & opt-out ladder: customer has requested a shorter notice window and a staggered opt-out for pilot SKUs. We need to settle on 30/45/60 day options and whether any premium refunds apply.
2) Termination for convenience (TFC): NovaHealth wants a mutual TFC with a 30‑day notice; legal prefers 60 days plus pro‑rated credits.
3) Data handoff & retention timeline post‑termination: procurement flagged 90 days, but infra prefers a 30 day snapshot + 14 day secure pull window.
4) Fallback routing: clarify if Redwood can map to a lower‑tier hosted model when Dedicated capacity is removed (operational SLA implications).

Ask: Karthik — can you take the redline and propose compromise language focused on: 45 day notice, mutual TFC with pro‑rated refund for prepaid months, and a 45/30 data handoff window? Marissa — please confirm operational impact and whether we can commit to a 14‑day live support handover.

Samantha — thanks for the earlier comments in the spreadsheet; if we can align quickly on 45 days we should be able to keep the signed order form in this quarter.

Proposed next steps: legal redline by EOD Wednesday (12/2), internal ops feasibility by Thursday (12/3), commercial signoff and DocuSign prepped by Friday (12/4).

Best,
Logan
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: OF-Redline-v3.docx (redline), NovaHealth-Reqs.xlsx (procurement list)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Samantha Price <samantha.price@novahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — notice ladder, auto-renew escape, and TFC fallback

On Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 9:12 AM Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Attaching the latest order form redline (OF-Redline-v3.docx). Legal and procurement items left outstanding:
> 
> 1) Auto-renew trigger & opt-out ladder...

Thanks, Logan — I reviewed OF-Redline-v3 and added in-line suggestions (see attached). High-level recommendations: 

- Notice window: agree to a single 45‑day mutual notice for convenience termination. It balances NovaHealth's ask and our operational lead time.
- Auto-renew: replace hard auto‑renew with a rolling renewal that requires 45‑day written notice to opt out for annual SKUs; for pilot SKUs allow a 30‑day opt‑out with a 30% pilot fee clawback if earlier than 90 days.
- Pro‑rated refunds: we should offer pro‑rated refunds for unused full months; do not refund usage-based fees. Add explicit language describing calculation to avoid disputes.
- Data handoff: commit to a 45 day retention window post termination for production snapshots plus a 14 day secure export period for customers to pull data; include responsibility for egress costs if large (>5TB) unless agreed in advance.
- Fallback model routing: add operational carve-out that allows Redwood to reroute to a compatible hosted variant (same model family, lower performance tier) for 30 days while customer chooses replacement infra — we should limit this to non-confidential workloads or where customer explicitly approves.

I marked redline lines that require commercial signoff (refund mechanics, egress cost threshold). Happy to call into a quick sync with procurement if helpful.

-Karthik
Senior Counsel (Commercial)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: OF-Redline-v3_karthik-comments.docx

From: Samantha Price <samantha.price@novahealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: NovaHealth Procurement <procurement@novahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 08:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — notice ladder, auto-renew escape, and TFC fallback

Logan / Karthik,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the suggested 45 day compromise. A few clarifications from NovaHealth: 

- Procurement cannot accept any auto‑renew mechanic that reduces our ability to consolidate vendor reviews — we need a hard annual renewal unless there is a confirmed pilot SKU exception. If you must keep rolling renewals, NovaHealth requires a 60‑day notification for enterprise SKUs.
- For TFC, our internal counsel insists on a mutual right but with a 30 day minimum so we can spin down patient pipelines; however we can be flexible on the refund mechanics if Redwood agrees to a 90 day data retention for audit purposes (we are HIPAA‑sensitive).
- Egress: NovaHealth cannot absorb unbounded egress charges. We propose a shared cost model where Redwood covers the first 1TB of export and we split incremental costs up to 5TB; beyond that we agree to a quoted egress pass‑through.

I uploaded a short requirements workbook (NovaHealth-Reqs.xlsx) so you can see which SKUs are pilots vs enterprise. Can we set a 30 minute procurement/legal sync tomorrow to finalize language? Our preferred window is 10:00–11:30 PT.

Regards,
Samantha Price
Sr. Procurement Manager
NovaHealth

Attachment: NovaHealth-Reqs.xlsx

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@novahealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: NovaHealth Procurement <procurement@novahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — notice ladder, auto-renew escape, and TFC fallback

Thanks, Samantha — appreciate the clarity and the workbook. 

Summary / proposed compromise (so we have a single set of points for legal and procurement to sign off):

1) Renewal mechanics
   - Enterprise SKUs: annual term with 60‑day pre‑renewal notice required to opt out (NovaHealth request accepted).
   - Pilot SKUs: rolling 12 month term with 30‑day opt‑out; pilot fee clawback as Karthik proposed if terminated within first 90 days.

2) Termination for convenience (mutual)
   - Mutual TFC with 45‑day notice for enterprise; 30‑day for pilots. (This hybrid keeps operational lead time while addressing NovaHealth's need to spin down pilot pipelines faster.)

3) Data retention & egress
   - Redwood commits to 90 day retention for audit purposes (HIPAA‑sensitive) as NovaHealth asked.
   - Customer has a 14 day secure export window where Redwood will keep a production snapshot available.
   - Egress cost sharing: Redwood covers first 1TB free; incremental up to 5TB split 50/50; >5TB quoted pass‑through.

4) Fallback routing and SLA carve outs
   - Redwood may route to a compatible hosted variant for up to 30 days as temporary capacity fallback; require explicit customer approval if workload is marked confidential.

Next steps: I will capture the above in OF-Redline-v4 and share a DocuSign draft. Karthik — if you can incorporate the hybrid TFC language and the egress cost caps, we can run the procurement sync tomorrow at 10:30 PT and aim to eSign Friday. Marissa — ops OK with the 30 day template fallback? If yes, we'll add operational runbook (offramp-runbook-v1.pdf) to the contract annex.

If we all agree, I'll schedule the 30 minute sync for 10:30 PT tomorrow and circulate the updated redline by 9:30.

Best,
Logan
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: offramp-runbook-v1.pdf (operational annex)
